summary: Red team of the extraction of Balakrishnan–Dogra–Müller–Tuitman–Vonk, 'Explicit Chabauty–Kim for the split Cartan modular curve of level 13' (Ann. of Math. 189 (2019) 885–944). I read the published text in full; its hash matches the extraction, and arXiv v1 is the only preprint version. The extraction is careful. Every numbered statement has an item. The one library citation holds at the pins. E1–E8 are all real, and the review's corrections to E3 and E5 are right. I re-derived (45), the Teichmüller splitting and Lemma 5.7. There are nine findings, six medium and three low. (1) Nekovář's general p-adic height pairing and local heights (/24, /26, /27, /31) are now planned twice: NC.5 through this route, and the Part II SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights accepted a day later. (2) X_s(ℓ), X_ns(ℓ) and X_0^+(ℓ²) are not planned at Tau Ceti ModularCurves layer 10, whose class is prime-level diamond quotients only. The isomorphism /71 goes to a bad-fibre layer. (3) Besser's Frobenius-equivariant transport is not planned at ColemanIntegration L1. (4) /79's Gross–Zagier half conflicts with the accepted PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/304, which records it as missing. (5) Tuitman's algorithm, which produces F, f, the Hecke matrices and the Frobenius lifts, has no item. (6) Definition A.2 omits uniqueness, which makes its 'unique up to unique isomorphism' claim false; item /68 copies both. Low: the ℓ ∈ {2,3,5,7} half of Theorem 1.2 has no item; there are further misprints (Definition A.1, the [Nek93] DOI) and a gap in the proof of Corollary 6.7 away from 13; sourceVersions and review blocks are missing.

No finding here depends on that red team.

Sources. Published text: https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v189-n3-p06-s.pdf, fetched 30 September 2026, 60 pp., SHA-256 e1aa5f9662b4875404e25e45dd808e2b73223d562191018242ef357a13dff1f8, which matches the extraction. arXiv v1: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.05846v1, SHA-256 77c57b0307c8915959a771c15bc89c6c46ae4c2d3b344c81ce898cfa9b90c917, which matches. The arXiv abstract page lists v1 only. Crossref has no update for 10.4007/annals.2019.189.3.6: no 'updated-by', and the updates filter returns 0.

Reading. I read the whole published paper (pp. 885–944, including Appendix A and the references) in a text extraction with page markers. I rendered pp. 923 and 931 at 300 dpi. p. 923 confirms the review's correction to E3: the (3,1) entry prints ∫_{x_0}^{x} ω^T Zω beside ∫_x^{x_0} η. p. 931 confirms that Z_1 and Z_2 are antisymmetric with zero lower-right block, as conditions (d) and (b) require. I read arXiv v1 wherever a finding or a review claim turns on it: Definition A.2, Lemma 4.5 (⊗ Q_p, confirming the review's addition to E5), both displays of C_n (2g+2d−2, confirming E1's arXiv locator) and the [Nek93] entry.

Coverage. I matched every numbered statement of the published text to an item locator: Lemma 1.5, Theorems 1.1–1.2, Corollary 1.3, Remarks 1.4–1.7, Theorems 2.2–2.3, Lemma 2.4, Remarks 2.1 and 2.5, Definitions 3.1, 3.3 and 3.4, Lemma 3.2, Theorem 3.6, Lemma 3.7, Corollary 3.8, Remarks 3.5 and 3.9–3.12, Theorems 4.2, 4.5 and 4.11, Lemmas 4.3, 4.7 and 4.10, Corollary 4.4, Remarks 4.1, 4.6, 4.8 and 4.9, Lemmas 5.2, 5.4, 5.5 and 5.7, Theorem 5.3, Remarks 5.1 and 5.6, Proposition 6.2, Theorems 6.5–6.6, Corollary 6.7, Remarks 6.1, 6.3, 6.4, 6.8 and 6.9, Definitions A.1, A.2 and A.5, and Lemmas A.3–A.4. None is missing. Unnumbered inputs without an item are findings 3, 5 and 7.

Topics the job lists. Each has an item and the item is right: the genus-3 plane quartic model and the Baran substitution (/85), the seven rational points (/85, /5, /7), quadratic Chabauty pairs (/11–/13), Nekovář's heights (/24–/32), local heights at p through the Hodge filtration (/44–/53) and Frobenius (/54–/61), local heights away from p (/27–/28, /36; the only bad prime is 13, handled by /72–/76), r = g = 3 (/82), ρ = 3 > 1 (/77), and Serre uniformity (/2, /6). Two do not apply. The Mordell–Weil sieve is only mentioned: p.888 says it 'cannot be applied on its own'. Vologodsky integration and Kedlaya's algorithm are not used; Tuitman's algorithm is used, and that is finding 5. Local heights away from p come from Lemma 3.2 (inflation–restriction), not from intersection theory, which this paper does not use.

Mathematics re-derived. (45): the three blocks of Λ_φG + dG = GΛ give φ*ω = Fω + df, dg^T = df^T ZF (using F^TZF = pZ) and dh = ω^TF^TZf + df^TZf − g^Tω + φ*η − pη, as printed. The Teichmüller splitting (p.923) solves S = G S D with D = diag(1, F^{-1}, 1/p) and gives α = (I−F)^{-1}f, β^T = g^T(F−p)^{-1}, γ = (g^Tα + h)/(1−p), as printed. (I−F)^{-1}f(x_0) = ∫_{b_0}^{x_0}ω by Frobenius invariance, as in E3. Lemma 5.7: L·R^{-1}·M with Z antisymmetric gives the stated matrix. Theorem 6.6 and the genus formula: with (ℓ²−1)/2 = 12k(6k+1), the sum 3k² + (k−1)(3k−2) + 2k − 2 equals 6k² − 3k = (ℓ² − 8ℓ + 7)/24, which is 3 for ℓ = 13 and 45 for ℓ = 37. E4's reading of N = (0_g,1_g)^T as the inclusion of Fil⁰V_dR holds only for a basis with ω_0,…,ω_{g−1} holomorphic, as E4 says. Remark 6.9 and /88: rows of T_2 built from Z_1 data are right, because B = h is shared, so (1, −β) kills every row.

Recorded source issues E1–E8. I checked each at its locator in the published text and all eight are confirmed; each quotation matches the page. E3 was also checked on the page image and against (41) and (44). E5's retraction is as recorded (BDMTV 2023 §3.5.2 per the review; I did not re-fetch the sequel). E8 is right that dim H^1_f(G_T,V) = r + corank Sha[p^∞]. The review's two in-place changes are correct: E3's (3,1) entry and E5's arXiv ⊗ Q_p. The review's item-81 addition is checked below.

findings.claim: Nekovář's p-adic height pairing now has two owners. The extraction (23 September) found no p-adic height in the atlas and routed the general construction to NC.5: the pairing h on H^1_f(G_T,V) × H^1_f(G_T,V*(1)) under Nekovář's conditions (/24), its decomposition h = Σ_v h_v into local terms (/26), and the definitions of h_v for v ≠ p and of h_p through D_cris (/27, /31). The next day the accepted route 2 of PAPER-DISEGNI-LIU-24 created the Part II SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights (parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology). Its brief plans exactly this: Nekovář's pairing on H^1_f under (V1)–(V3), its decomposition into local terms and Nekovář's local index. Its first test is to recover, for a curve and degree-0 divisors, 'Nekovář's height pairing on Selmer groups of the Jacobian', which is the case these items describe. PAPER-DISEGNI-22 reuses the same Part II. So the general pairing and local heights are now planned once in the Part II and again in NC.5 through this route. PROTOCOL §15 says a general notion is planned once, in its most general form, in the most foundational roadmap. That is SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights, and NC.5 should import it. What stays specific to this paper, and belongs in NC.5, is the mixed extension A_Z(b,x), twisting, (θ, Υ), Lemma 3.7 and Corollary 3.8, and the explicit formula (17) for V = H^1_ét(X)^*.

findings.claim: The curves X_s(ℓ), X_ns(ℓ) and X_0^+(ℓ²) that the whole paper is about are not planned where the extraction says. Item /1's note claims that Tau Ceti ModularCurves layer 10 compactifies X_H with cusps, with 'X_s(ℓ) and X_ns(ℓ) … instances'. Layer 10 says the opposite. Its class is fixed once as the diamond quotients Y_1(N)/H of prime level N ≥ 5, 'and not arbitrary finite quotients of Layer 9, for which none of the assertions below is made'. Layer 9 plans only the affine quotient problems over Ell. Its regularity theorems cover the semi-Borel and product subgroups of the diagonal Cartan, not the normaliser C_s(ℓ)^+ or a non-split Cartan normaliser. So the projective curves X_s(ℓ) and X_ns(ℓ), their cusps, and the moduli meaning of a non-cuspidal rational point are all unplanned. Theorem 1.1 counts a cusp among the seven points and needs all three. X_0^+(ℓ²) is also unplanned: it is composite level, and it is a quotient of X_0(ℓ²) by w_{ℓ²}, while layer 10 extends w_N only at prime level. The one proposed layer that constructs coarse compactified curves beyond layer 10's class is ModularCurvesPartII R13.4a. Its text lists 'full, fixed-pairing, Γ₁ and refined Γ₀ level'. Item /71 then sends the Q-isomorphism X_0^+(ℓ²) ≃ X_s(ℓ), a statement about generic fibres, to R13.5, 'Bad fibres and regular/semistable models', which is the wrong owner.
findings.evidence: Atlas stage tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#layer-10-…: 'In this layer **the standard problems** are the diamond-operator quotients of `[Γ₁(N)]` and nothing else: for `N ≥ 5` **prime** … Every unqualified `Y_H`, `X_H`, `Cusps_H` in this layer quantifies over exactly this class — not the seven identifications of 9B as a list, and not arbitrary finite quotients of Layer 9, for which none of the assertions below is made.' Layer 9 (KM 7.6.1): 'the quotients of [Γ(p^n)] by subgroups of the semi-Borel or by product subgroups H₁×H₂ of the diagonal Cartan are regular'. ModularCurvesPartII:R13.4a: 'Construct coarse compactified curves … Treat full, fixed-pairing, Γ₁ and refined Γ₀ level separately'. R13.5: 'Compute the local models and supersingular intersections …'. Paper p.887: 'we write X_s(ℓ) for the modular curve X(ℓ)/C_s(ℓ)^+'; p.926: 'there is a Q-isomorphism X_0^+(ℓ²) ≃ X_s(ℓ) coming from conjugation with (ℓ 0; 0 1), where X_0^+(ℓ²) is the quotient of X_0(ℓ²) by the Atkin-Lehner involution w_{ℓ²}'; Theorem 1.1 (p.888): 'six CM points and one cusp'.
findings.fix: Make /1 missing and route it, with /71, by a source route to ModularCurvesPartII:R13.4a. That layer then gains the compactified coarse curves X(ℓ)/H for H = C_s(ℓ)^+ and C_ns(ℓ)^+ over Q, the curve X_0(ℓ²) and its quotient by w_{ℓ²}, the isomorphism of /71, and the criterion that a non-cuspidal rational point comes from an E/Q whose mod-ℓ image lies in a conjugate of H (up to twist at j = 0, 1728). Cite layer 9 (9A quotients) as the affine input and layer 10 only for the prime-level Γ_0 case. Take /71 out of route 4. Route 4 keeps /72–/76, which do concern bad fibres.

findings.claim: Item /58 bundles two statements, and only the first is planned. The first is the formal-integration formula I(x_1,x_2) with the transport τ_{b,x}(v) = I(x_0,x)·v·I(b,b_0) on a residue disk, (40)–(41). The second is Besser's theorem: with Coleman integrals in (40), the same formula is the unique unipotent Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism A_n^dR(b_0,x_0) → A_n^dR(b,x) for arbitrary b, b_0, x, x_0. That second statement is what makes the §5.3.2 splitting, Lemma 5.7 and §6.6 work. ColemanIntegration L1 plans Coleman functions, iterated Coleman integrals (the word algebra) and Frobenius equivariance of integration, which covers the first. It does not plan Frobenius-equivariant parallel transport on unipotent connections or path torsors. It avoids the Tannakian formulation on purpose: 'so that no general Tannakian theorem is an unowned prerequisite'. The reviewed ColemanIntegration packet has no node on transport, path torsors or unipotent isocrystals; I searched its node titles and statements. So the report's description of L1 is wrong, and Besser's theorem is missing.
findings.evidence: Atlas stage ColemanIntegration:L1: 'Define Coleman functions … Build pullback, differentiation, products and integration … For the application to P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, provide a direct construction by successive extensions, so that no general Tannakian theorem is an unowned prerequisite.' research/blueprint/packets/ColemanIntegration.json: nodes L1/word-algebra, L1/coleman-realization, L1/coleman-integral and L1/coleman-integration-characterisation; no node mentions transport, a path torsor or a unipotent isocrystal. Paper p.921, §5.2.1: 'By Besser's theory of Coleman integration on unipotent connections [Bes02], we have that for any b, b_0, x, x_0 ∈ Y(Q_p), the same formula (41) describes the unique unipotent Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism A_n^dR(b_0,x_0) → A_n^dR(b,x) if the integrals in formula (40) are instead interpreted in the sense of Coleman integration.'

(b) Add a missing theorem item for Besser's result [Bes02]: Frobenius-equivariant unipotent parallel transport exists and is unique, and in the trivialisation (39) it is given by (41) with Coleman integrals. findings.claim: The computation behind Theorem 1.1 relies on Tuitman's algorithm at three points, and no item states it. First, the Frobenius structure: F and the overconvergent functions f with φ*ω = Fω + df, which enter (45), are computed and then (45) is solved. Second, the Hecke matrices: Fr_q on H^1_dR(X_{Q_q}), for q = 3, 7, 11, gives A_q through (50) and so the Tate classes Z_1, Z_2 and the K-action. Third, the Frobenius lifts Φ(x) = x^p on strict neighbourhoods of ]U_1[ and ]U_2[. Items /60, /84 and /87 take these outputs as given; /87 cites [Tui16] only for the existence of the lift. The algorithm's statement is missing: for a plane model monic in y with a map x: X → P¹, it constructs an overconvergent Frobenius lift and reduces φ*ω in H^1_rig(U) to the basis ω plus an exact form, with explicit p-adic precision bounds. Without it ED.6 has no certified way to produce F, f, A_q or the lifts. Nothing else in the atlas plans it: RD.7 only asks that 'Certified point-count algorithms must include precision and integral-reconstruction bounds', and CN.3 plans modular symbols and point counts, not Frobenius on rigid cohomology.
findings.evidence: Paper p.924: 'The Frobenius structure is computed explicitly on the Teichmüller representative x_0 of x using the algorithms of Tuitman [Tui16], [Tui17] to solve the system of equations (45)'; p.930: 'Using the algorithms of [Tui16], [Tui17], we can compute the matrix of Fr_q with respect to the basis ω to any desired precision. Then (50) allows us to compute the matrix A_q of T_q'; p.931: 'We apply the methods of [Tui16] to define a lift Φ of Frobenius on a strict open neighbourhood of ]U_1[ satisfying Φ(x) = x^p'; p.933: 'As our model is monic in v, we can again apply the methods of [Tui16]'. findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19.result.json: item PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/68 (Universal pointed objects) and sourceIssues (no entry); research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19.md, 'Mistakes found'
findings.claim: Definition A.2 omits the uniqueness of the morphism. It asks only that a morphism (E,e) → (V,v) exist. The paper then says 'if a universal pointed n-unipotent object exists, it is unique up to unique isomorphism', and item /68 copies both. Under the printed definition that claim is false. Take n ≥ 0 and set E' = A_n(C,ω) ⊕ 1, with e' = (1,0) and filtration E'_0 = A_n ⊕ 1, E'_i = I^iA_n for i ≥ 1; it is pointed n-unipotent. For any pointed n-unipotent (V,v), compose the projection E' → A_n, which respects filtrations and sends e' to 1, with the morphism (A_n,1) → (V,v). So (E',e') is 'universal', but ω(E') has dimension dim A_n + 1, so it is not isomorphic to (A_n,1). The proofs need uniqueness. Lemma 5.2's proof says 'As explained in Section A.1, a morphism of n-unipotent universal objects is determined by where it sends 1'. Lemma A.4's proof uses the bijection Hom(ω_n,ν_n) ≅ ν(A_n(C,ω)). Theorem 4.2 does say 'there exists a unique map'. So the intended definition is clear (Kim's), and this is a misprint that affects nothing, but the extraction neither records it nor corrects /68. arXiv v1 has the same wording.
findings.evidence: Paper p.935, Definition A.2: 'We say a pointed n-unipotent object (E, e) is a universal pointed n-unipotent object if for all pointed n-unipotent objects (V, v), there exists a morphism of pointed n-unipotent objects (E, e) −→ (V, v).' Next paragraph: 'Note that if a universal pointed n-unipotent object exists, it is unique up to unique isomorphism.' p.919, proof of Lemma 5.2: 'As explained in Section A.1, a morphism of n-unipotent universal objects is determined by where it sends 1 ∈ b*A_n^rig(b), which shows uniqueness.' p.936, proof of Lemma A.4: 'By the universal property of A_n, the map Hom(ω_n, ν_n) → ν(A_n(C, ω)), F ↦ F(A_n)(e_n) is an isomorphism'. arXiv v1 p.34 (Definition A.2) is identical. Item /68 statement: '(E, e) is a universal pointed n-unipotent object if it maps to every pointed n-unipotent (V, v) … Such objects are unique up to unique isomorphism.'
findings.fix: Add sourceIssue E9 (misprint, affects nothing, known: new; searched arXiv 1711.05846 (v1 only), Crossref (no update) and the Annals article page). Printed: 'there exists a morphism'; correction: 'there exists a unique morphism'; reason: the counterexample (A_n ⊕ 1, (1,0)) above. Restate /68 with 'a unique morphism' and note the correction.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19.result.json: item PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/6 (Theorem 1.2) and its note ('Theorem 1.1 plus the cited Bilu–Parent–Rebolledo theorem (ℓ > 7, ℓ ≠ 13) and ℓ = 11 inside it')
findings.claim: Theorem 1.2 says the set of primes is exactly {2, 3, 5, 7}. The note accounts only for the exclusion of ℓ ≥ 11. For the inclusion of 2, 3, 5, 7, non-CM curves must exist: X_s(ℓ) ≅ X_0^+(ℓ²) has genus 0 for these ℓ and has a rational cusp, so it is P¹ over Q. It therefore has infinitely many rational points, of which finitely many are CM or cusps. Each remaining point gives an E/Q, after a twist, with image in C_s(ℓ)^+. The paper does not say this. Neither item /6 nor any other item covers it, although item /75's genus formula covers only ℓ ≡ 1 mod 12.
findings.evidence: Paper p.888, Theorem 1.2: 'The set of primes ℓ for which there exists an elliptic curve E/Q without CM such that ρ_{E,ℓ} is contained in the normaliser of a split Cartan subgroup is {2, 3, 5, 7}.' The only justification in the paper is p.888: 'Together with the results of Bilu–Parent and Bilu–Parent–Rebolledo, this allows us to complete the characterisation', and BPR (p.887) concerns ℓ > 7.
findings.fix: Add to /6 (or as a new theorem item routed with it to ED.6) the statement: for ℓ ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7}, X_s(ℓ)(Q) is infinite and contains a non-CM non-cuspidal point. Note that the paper leaves this to the reader. It needs genus 0 and a rational point on X_0^+(ℓ²), plus the moduli criterion of the reworked /1.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19.result.json: sourceIssues (missed misprints and one gap), items PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/67 and /76, and the prerequisites entry for Nekovář 1993
findings.claim: The published text has more mistakes than the eight recorded. (1) Definition A.1 says 'C is unipotent if every object V ∈ C admits a nonzero morphism 1 → V'. That fails for V = 0; it should say every nonzero object. Item /67 copies it. (2) The bibliography's DOI for [Nek93] is wrong. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-005-0696-y is van der Laan, Talman and Yang, 'Solving discrete zero point problems', Mathematical Programming (2006). Nekovář's chapter is 10.1007/978-1-4757-4271-8_8, which the extraction's prerequisites list uses without saying the printed DOI differs. The same list prints [BL04] as 'Complex Abelian Barieties'. (3) The proof of Corollary 6.7 derives 'good reduction outside 13' from Theorem 6.6, which concerns only the prime ℓ = 13. Good reduction at the other primes comes from elsewhere. One route is the first plane model of §6.3, which the paper says 'has good reduction away from 13' (and which the review checked). Another is smoothness of X_0(169) over Z[1/13] and of its quotient. At 2 the quotient needs its own argument, since the H^1(⟨w⟩, m) step of Theorem 6.6's proof uses that 2 is invertible. Item /76 inherits the gap. None of these affects a result.
findings.evidence: Paper p.934, Definition A.1: 'Equivalently, C is unipotent if every object V ∈ C admits a nonzero morphism 1 −→ V from the unit object 1 in C.' p.943, [Nek93]: '… Progr. Math. 108, Birkhäuser Boston, Boston, MA, 1993, pp. 127–202 … https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-005-0696-y'. Crossref, read 30 September 2026: 10.1007/s10107-005-0696-y is 'Solving discrete zero point problems', Mathematical Programming, 2006; 10.1007/978-1-4757-4271-8_8 is 'On p-adic height pairings', Séminaire de Théorie des Nombres, Paris, 1990–91. p.940: '[BL04] C. Indeed, we may contract all three rational curves to obtain a smooth model over W[ϖ].' p.930: the first model 'has good reduction away from 13'. arXiv v1's [Nek93] entry carries no DOI.
